c.tagline: East Africa's oldest and best-preserved Swahili town, a car-free island of coral-stone alleys and donkey traffic

card: Accepted at larger hotels; cash and M-Pesa mobile money preferred elsewhere
rides: donkeys (the island's main form of local transport)

taxi.color: not applicable (no motorized vehicles on the island)
taxi.fare: Boat and donkey transport negotiated locally
taxi.fareNote: Lamu Island bans cars; getting around is by foot, donkey, or dhow boat

emergency.note: 999/112 reaches police, fire, and ambulance across Kenya; medical facilities on Lamu are basic, with Mombasa as the nearest major hospital

religion: Islam (Sunni majority, reflecting Swahili coastal heritage)

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Lamu Old Town is entirely car-free and walkable, though narrow and maze-like; Shela and other beaches are a walk or short dhow ride away

safety.safety: Generally safe within Lamu town and Shela; check current travel advisories for mainland areas near the Kenya-Somalia border before planning travel to the wider region
safety.crime: Low crime on the island itself; standard coastal-destination caution applies

hood_landmark.Lamu Old Town: Lamu Fort and the winding coral-stone alleys of the old town
hood_landmark.Shela: Shela's long sandy beach and boutique guesthouses
hood_landmark.Kipungani: Kipungani's quiet southern-tip beaches and mangroves
hood_landmark.Manda Island (day-trip): Manda Island's Takwa ruins and Manda Bay beaches

avoid.reason: Coastal areas near the Somalia border carry a terrorism advisory — check before travel

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed heart of Lamu, a maze of narrow coral-stone lanes lined with carved wooden doors and centuries-old houses; the essential base for any visit.
A short walk or donkey ride from Lamu town, a quieter village with a long beach and Lamu's most upscale guesthouses.
The bustling dhow-lined harbor where boats arrive and depart, lined with cafes and a good spot to watch daily island life.
A remote, sparsely populated stretch on the island's southern tip, reached by boat, offering total quiet and mangrove scenery.
A neighboring island reached by dhow, home to the Takwa ruins and quieter beaches than Lamu's own.

water.note: Drink bottled water; island wells are brackish and untreated.

transit.sys: Donkeys and foot traffic within Lamu town; dhow boats between islands
transit.pay: Cash or M-Pesa mobile money for boat fares
transit.map: Not applicable given the car-free island layout
transit.note: Lamu Island has no cars; donkeys and dhows are the primary modes of transport, a rarity in the modern world

transport.air: Manda Airport (LAU), reached by a short dhow crossing to Lamu Island, with domestic flights from Nairobi and Mombasa
transport.train: No passenger rail service to Lamu
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect to Mombasa (about 6-8 hr) via mainland roads
transport.ferry: Dhow and speedboat transfers connect Manda Airport to Lamu Island
transport.car: Not applicable; Lamu Island itself has no cars

airport.name: Manda Airport
airport.distance: Short dhow crossing (10-15 min) from Lamu town
airport.transport: Dhow or speedboat transfer, arranged by hotels

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in hotels
net.ap: A Safaricom tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: 10% is appreciated for boat operators and guides
tip.r: 10% is standard, though often added automatically at resort restaurants
